issues: wms/orders.py so_confirm runs the credit-limit check only after it has already written new unit_price/gross/net values into so_lines, so its claim to change nothing depends entirely on the outer transaction rolling back; the check should come before any UPDATE.

wms/catalog.py product_archive pulls in ledger, orders and purchasing through imports inside the function and replays the whole movement log (current_stock) plus one po_status/so_status call per order, so the catalog module now depends on most of the domain and does N+1 work.

wms/http.py patch calls ctx.live_product itself before the If-Match handling, which duplicates the archived check that product_edit already does and puts domain validation in the HTTP layer just to get the error order right.

wms/pricing.py parse_limit accepts 'none', so customer_add has to reject 'none' again with its own special case; parsing 'set or clear' and parsing 'a positive amount' are mixed together, which makes the validation easy to get wrong.

tests/test_archive_credit.py has no test that return create is rejected for an archived product, none for credit totals on backordered or partially_shipped orders or with an order discount, and none that a rejected archive or confirm leaves the database unchanged; the HTTP test also waits on a fixed time.sleep(1.5), which makes it flaky.

wms/http.py products_page treats any archived value other than '1' or 'true' as false without an error, and wms/orders.py so_confirm computes the committed total with one so_status replay per order of the customer, which will get slow on large books.
strengths: The --at bug is fixed at its cause: reports.cut_for uses 'at<=?', and both valuation and stock_report get the cutoff from this one helper, so every affected report is fixed together.

The archive guard is centralised in Ctx.live_product and used at each booking entry point (receive, adjust, po/so create, price set, promo add, return create, product edit), while read paths keep using ctx.product, so history stays intact.
The optional keys (archived, credit_limit) are only added when set, which keeps existing output unchanged, and session.migrate upgrades older books in place; there is a test for that migration.
